label: rem:leray-profile-construction
title: Truncations of the Leray system for a discretely self-similar profile
html:
The Leray rescaling. In Leray's similarity variables y = (x - x_0)/\sqrt{T^* - t}, s = -\log(T^* - t), the velocity profile satisfies the Leray system. A continuous self-similar blowup would require a time-independent (s-independent) profile (V, \Pi) on \mathbb{R}^3; such a profile with V \in L^3(\mathbb{R}^3) is zero [necas-ruzicka-sverak1996], a no-go extended to L^q, 3 < q \leq \infty, and to local-energy estimates [tsai1998]. The profile considered here is therefore discretely self-similar: periodic in s with some period P > 0. The Leray system itself does not fix P.

The period. An identification of P with the scaling \lambda_\kappa of the root-of-unity ladder q_\kappa = e^{i\pi/\kappa} would require evaluating at a root of unity, which the substrate parameter excludes. No identification of P is made here.

The angular decomposition. A velocity field on \mathbb{R}^3 decomposes in angle into vector spherical harmonics of integer degree \ell: the sphere is S^2 = \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1), and functions or vector fields on it carry only integer spin. Half-integer components j = 1/2, 3/2, \ldots do not occur in a Navier--Stokes velocity field. The quadratic term (V \cdot \nabla) V couples degrees \ell_1 and \ell_2 to every degree \ell with |\ell_1 - \ell_2| \le \ell \le \ell_1 + \ell_2, so a finite set of degrees is in general not closed under the nonlinearity.

Truncation. Consequently a truncation at finitely many degrees \ell \le L is a Galerkin approximation of the Leray system, not an exact reduction. A discretely self-similar profile depends on s periodically; after expansion in Fourier modes in s, the truncated system is a system of ODEs in the radial variable r indexed by both the angular degree and the Fourier mode. A truncation keeping only the zero Fourier mode is s-independent and is the steady case excluded above.

Boundary conditions. Each radial coefficient must be regular at r = 0, with the vanishing order set by its degree \ell and the type of vector spherical harmonic. At r \to \infty the profile must decay like r^{-1} and no faster. Decay faster than r^{-1} puts a bounded profile in L^3, and a discretely self-similar blow-up whose profile is continuous in s with values in L^3 is excluded [chae2013adss]; in particular a bounded square-integrable profile lies in L^3 and is excluded. Decay slower than r^{-1} makes the velocity field unbounded away from the blow-up point. See Exclusions for discretely self-similar profiles.

Open question. The coefficients of the truncated system are not specified here. Writing them down from the vector-spherical-harmonic coupling, and then deciding whether a nonzero s-periodic solution exists and persists as L grows, is the open content of this construction. Any numerical solution of a truncated system is evidence about the truncation, not about the Leray system.
